content:
Ads will launch this summer in the United States and Canada on Apple Maps. Ahead of the rollout, Apple has released further details on what is allowed and prohibited in Apple Maps advertising.

Apple Maps ads are about to arrive, and Apple has simultaneously revealed the categories that are banned from running.

Apple first announced plans to introduce advertising in Apple Maps back in March, saying at the time that ads would appear at the top of search results, as well as in a new “Suggested Places” widget within the app.

Apple rolled out the underlying infrastructure for this in May with iOS 26.5, including the new “Suggested Places” feature. But the company has not shared any further updates on the official launch of Apple Maps ads since then.

According to TechCrunch, Apple has now updated its “Apple Advertising Services” policies with new content related to Apple Maps.

The policy covers the overall advertising guidelines for Apple services such as News, Stocks, and Maps, and includes a lengthy list of prohibited content applicable to ads across all services, including items such as violence, weapons, and drugs.

Most notably, the policy further reveals specific restrictions for Apple Maps ads. Apple says there are three additional categories banned specifically for Apple Maps advertising:

  • Home services: No ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes home services, including but not limited to plumbing, locksmiths, HVAC, pest control, roofing, or general contracting services.
  • Bail bonds: No ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes bail bond services or surety services related to criminal pre-trial release.
  • Crypto ATMs: No ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes cryptocurrency ATMs.

In addition, Apple says ads related to medical services will be evaluated on a “case-by-case basis.”

As TechCrunch points out, Apple’s ban on the entire “home services” category is quite noteworthy. This is a major advertising category on Google Maps, but Apple clearly has no interest in it.

All signs point to Apple preparing to launch ads on Apple Maps imminently, but as of now there is still no official launch date.

The full list of prohibited ad categories is available on Apple’s official website.
